item.title: Starting an online study group
item.context_text: You are preparing for an international English exam with an online course. The final test is in six weeks. You want to start a small online study group with three classmates who live in different cities and time zones.
item.objective_text: Understand the course rules for group work, agree a time that suits everyone, invite your classmates in writing and explain the plan in the first call.
item.target_grammar: suggestions and making plans (How about…? Why don't we…? Let's…, We could…)
item.cultural_note: In online groups across time zones, always give times with the city or time zone ("8 pm Tashkent time"). Giving everyone a clear role from the start stops one person from doing all the work.
success_conditions: Understand what the course allows in group work
Find a time that works for every member
Write a clear invitation with time, time zone and roles
Explain the plan and check everyone agrees

children.title: Read the course forum post
children.instructions: Read this post from your course tutor. Then answer the questions.
children.prompt_text:
Study groups – a few rules
We really encourage you to practise together! You may share notes, practise speaking and check each other's essays. However, the weekly graded tasks must be your own work: please don't share answers to these.
Groups of three to five work best. If you start a group, post the day and time in this forum so other students can join.

questions.prompt: What must students NOT do in study groups?
options: Share answers to the graded tasks
questions.explanation: "The weekly graded tasks must be your own work: please don't share answers to these."

questions.prompt: What does the tutor ask group organisers to do?
options: Post the day and time in the forum
Send the tutor a list of members
Keep the group to two people
questions.explanation: "Post the day and time in this forum so other students can join."

children.title: Listen to your classmates
children.instructions: You ask your three classmates when they are free. Listen to their voice messages. Then answer the questions.
children.prompt_text:
Maya: Hi! I'm in Berlin, so I'm four hours behind Tashkent. Weekday evenings are fine for me after six, my time.
Kenji: Hello from Seoul! I'm four hours ahead of Tashkent. I go to bed early, so anything after eleven at night, my time, is too late. Weekends are easier.
Omar: Hi, it's Omar in Cairo. I work on Saturdays, but Sunday is completely free for me.

questions.explanation: "I work on Saturdays, but Sunday is completely free for me."

questions.prompt: What is Kenji's problem with late meetings?
questions.explanation: "I go to bed early, so anything after eleven at night, my time, is too late."

questions.prompt: Which day seems best for everyone?
questions.explanation: Kenji prefers weekends and Omar works on Saturdays, so Sunday works for all.

children.title: Write the invitation
children.instructions: Write a message to the three classmates. Suggest a day and time (with a time zone), say what you will do in each session, and suggest a role for each person.
children.goal: Invite the group with a clear time, plan and roles.

points.label: give a time with a time zone

children.model_answer: Hi Maya, Kenji and Omar! Thanks for your messages. Sunday seems best for everyone, so how about every Sunday at 3 pm Tashkent time? That's 11 am in Berlin, noon in Cairo and 7 pm in Seoul. Let's spend the first half on speaking practice and the second half checking each other's essays. Maya, could you keep the time? Kenji, could you share a document for notes? Omar and I can take turns choosing the speaking topics. What do you think?

children.title: Explain the plan in the first call
children.instructions: The first video call starts. Welcome everyone, explain the plan in a few sentences, mention the tutor's rule about graded tasks, and check that everyone agrees.
children.prompt_text: Maya: Hi everyone! So, what's the plan?
children.goal: Explain the plan clearly and check agreement.

points.label: mention the rule about graded tasks

children.model_answer: Hi everyone, welcome! So, the plan is to meet every Sunday for an hour. First we'll do thirty minutes of speaking practice, then we'll check each other's essays. Just remember the tutor's rule: we can't share answers to the graded tasks, they must be our own work. Does that work for everyone?
